draft.title: Number systems and sets
card: Number systems

Natural numbers ℕ are 1, 2, 3, and so on. Integers ℤ add 0 and the negatives. Rationals ℚ are numbers that can be written as a/b with a and b integers and b ≠ 0. Reals ℝ include every point on the number line, such as √2 and π.
Nesting
Each system sits inside the next: ℕ ⊂ ℤ ⊂ ℚ ⊂ ℝ. Complex numbers ℂ contain all the reals and also numbers such as √(−1).
Sets
A ∪ B (union) has everything in A or B or both. A ∩ B (intersection) has only what is in both. The complement A′ has everything in the universal set that is not in A.
Subset
A ⊆ B means every element of A is also in B. Example: A = {1, 2, 3, 4} and B = {3, 4, 5}. Then A ∪ B = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5} and A ∩ B = {3, 4}.
draft.remember: Each number system sits inside the next. Union is in either, intersection is in both.

a.q: If A = {2, 4, 6, 8} and B = {4, 8, 10}, what is A ∩ B?
a.why: The intersection holds only the elements that are in both sets, which are 4 and 8. The option {2, 4, 6, 8, 10} is the union, which holds everything in either set.
a.clue: Which numbers appear in both lists?

b.q: Which statement about number systems is true?
opts: The number 0.75 is rational but not an integer
The number √2 is rational because it is real
Every integer is a natural number
The number 3/4 is an integer because it is a fraction
b.why: 0.75 = 3/4 is a ratio of integers, so it is rational, and it is not a whole number, so it is not an integer. The number √2 is real but cannot be written as a/b. Negative integers are not natural numbers, so the third option is false.
b.clue: Check each number against the a/b test, and whether the nesting runs in that direction.

b.best: The number 0.75 is rational but not an integer

problems.detail: The 'Subset' bullet defines A ⊆ B, then gives an example where A = {1, 2, 3, 4} is not a subset of B = {3, 4, 5}. The example shows union and intersection instead, so a student could think it illustrates a subset. Use an example of an actual subset, or move this example to the Sets bullet.

final.title: Number systems and sets
card: Number systems

Natural numbers \(\mathbb{N}\) are 1, 2, 3, and so on. Integers \(\mathbb{Z}\) add 0 and the negatives. Rationals \(\mathbb{Q}\) are numbers that can be written as \(\frac{a}{b}\) with \(a\) and \(b\) integers and \(b \ne 0\). Reals \(\mathbb{R}\) include every point on the number line, such as \(\sqrt{2}\) and \(\pi\).
Nesting
Each system sits inside the next: \(\mathbb{N} \subset \mathbb{Z} \subset \mathbb{Q} \subset \mathbb{R}\). Complex numbers \(\mathbb{C}\) contain all the reals and also numbers such as \(\sqrt{-1}\).
Sets
\(A \cup B\) (union) has everything in \(A\) or \(B\) or both. \(A \cap B\) (intersection) has only what is in both. The complement \(A'\) has everything in the universal set that is not in \(A\).
Subset
\(A \subseteq B\) means every element of \(A\) is also in \(B\). Example: \(\{3, 4\} \subseteq \{2, 3, 4, 5\}\), but \(\{1, 3\}\) is not a subset of it, because 1 is missing.
final.remember: Each number system sits inside the next. Union is in either, intersection is in both.

a.why: The intersection holds only the elements that are in both sets, which are 4 and 8. The option \(\{2, 4, 6, 8, 10\}\) is the union, which holds everything in either set.
a.clue: Which numbers appear in both lists?

b.q: Which statement about number systems is true?
opts: 0.75 is rational but not an integer
\(\sqrt{2}\) is rational because it is a real number
Every integer is also a natural number
\(\frac{3}{4}\) is an integer because it is a ratio
b.why: \(0.75 = \frac{3}{4}\) is a ratio of integers, so it is rational, and it is not a whole number, so it is not an integer. The number \(\sqrt{2}\) is real but cannot be written as \(\frac{a}{b}\). Negative integers are not natural numbers, so the nesting does not run that way.
b.clue: Check each number against the \(\frac{a}{b}\) test, and which way the nesting runs.
